name: N01 normalizeDelayMs: only a negative reads as zero
why: NaN passes through as NaN (and -0 as -0); killed by the NaN and minus-zero rows of normalizeDelayMs and by the debouncer rows that read the delay the timer is asked for

name: N02 normalizeDelayMs: zero is kept, so minus zero is too
why: minus zero is returned as minus zero (Object.is), killed by the minus-zero rows (a timer is never handed a minus zero)

name: N03 normalizeDelayMs: a non-positive delay reads as one millisecond
why: zero, negative and NaN delays ask the timer for 1 ms; killed by the zero-delay and negative-delay rows

name: N04 normalizeDelayMs: the longest delay is capped from its own value
why: EQUIVALENT: at ms === MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS both spellings answer MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS (the cap and the value are the same number), and every other value falls on the same side of both comparisons

name: N05 normalizeDelayMs: no cap
why: a delay past what a host timer holds (Infinity, 2^31, a year) is handed through; killed by the cap rows

name: N06 MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS is 2^31
why: the constant row, and the cap rows that read the value one past it

name: N07 normalizeDelayMs: a fraction is floored
why: 1.5 becomes 1 and 0.25 becomes 0; killed by the fraction rows (the host's timer rounds, not this)

name: N08 normalizeDelayMs: the cap sits at 2^40
why: 2^31 and a year pass through uncapped; killed by the 'one past it' and 'a year' rows

name: N09 TYPING_DEBOUNCE_MS is 200
why: the constant row, and the sizes row of the clock rows

name: N10 realTimers.setTimeout ignores the delay
why: the host-timer row that sets a late and an early timer and reads the order they run in

name: N11 realTimers.clearTimeout does nothing
why: the host-timer row that clears a timer and reads that it did not run

name: D01 createKeyedDebouncer: the delay is not normalized
why: the timer is asked for NaN, a negative, minus zero, Infinity as given; killed by the delay rows of the debouncer

name: D02 createKeyedDebouncer: no default error report
why: a throwing run is swallowed silently; killed by the 'without an onError' rows (console.error is spied on)

name: D03 createKeyedDebouncer: schedule works after dispose
why: a schedule after dispose sets a timer and runs; killed by the dispose rows (no run, no timer)

name: D04 createKeyedDebouncer: a schedule does not drop the pending run
why: every schedule of a burst runs; killed by every burst row

name: D05 createKeyedDebouncer: a run leaves its entry in the table
why: the table keeps the handle of a timer that has run, and the next schedule or cancel of the key clears it (a stale clear); killed by the rows that count stale clears

name: D06 createKeyedDebouncer: a throwing run is not caught
why: the error leaves the timer and, on the fake clock, stops the rest of the advance; killed by the throw-isolation rows

name: D07 createKeyedDebouncer: a caught error is not reported
why: the throw rows read what onError received

name: D08 createKeyedDebouncer: cancel clears whether or not anything is pending
why: a cancel (and so a first schedule) of an absent key clears a handle that is not there; killed by the rows that count stale clears

name: D09 createKeyedDebouncer: cancel keeps the entry
why: a second cancel of the key clears the handle again (a stale clear); killed by the stale-clear row

name: D10 createKeyedDebouncer: dispose does not mark the debouncer disposed
why: later schedules after dispose set timers and run; killed by the dispose rows

name: D11 createKeyedDebouncer: dispose leaves the timers set
why: the pending runs still fire after dispose; killed by the dispose rows

name: D12 createKeyedDebouncer: dispose leaves the table full
why: a cancel after dispose clears a handle that was already cleared (a stale clear); killed by the stale-clear row

name: D13 createKeyedDebouncer: the timer is asked for no delay
why: every run is due at the next turn; killed by the delay rows and every pause row

name: D14 createKeyedDebouncer: one slot for every key
why: the table holds only the latest handle, so a schedule of another key cannot drop the first key's timer, and a cancel cannot find it; killed by the independence and cancel rows

name: D15 createKeyedDebouncer: a run empties the whole table
why: the other keys' handles are forgotten, so a dispose from inside a run leaves them set; killed by the dispose-from-inside row and the model differential

name: D16 createKeyedDebouncer: the default report goes to console.warn
from: console.error("Quarto: a debounced typing-path run failed", error);
to: console.warn("Quarto: a debounced typing-path run failed", error);
why: the 'without an onError' rows spy on console.error

name: S01 createCellContextScheduler: the evaluated version is never recorded
why: no event is ever 'the same version', so a cursor move is debounced; killed by the cursor-move rows

name: S02 createCellContextScheduler: the version is recorded before the evaluation
why: a failed evaluation is taken for done and the next event is not retried; killed by the throw rows

name: S03 createCellContextScheduler: the version is read after the evaluation
why: an edit that lands during the evaluation is recorded as evaluated; killed by the 'version the evaluation saw' row

name: S04 createCellContextScheduler: no editor is not a reason to evaluate at once
why: reading .key of an undefined snapshot throws; killed by the no-active-editor rows

name: S05 createCellContextScheduler: a first event compares with nothing
why: reading .key of an undefined evaluation throws; killed by the 'before anything was evaluated' row

name: S06 createCellContextScheduler: any document at the same version counts as evaluated
from: evaluated !== undefined && evaluated.key === now.key && evaluated.version === now.version
why: a switch the scheduler did not hear about is taken for evaluated; killed by the different-document row

name: S07 createCellContextScheduler: a different version counts as evaluated
why: typing is evaluated at once and a cursor move is debounced; killed by the burst and cursor-move rows

name: S08 createCellContextScheduler: a version not above the evaluated one counts as evaluated
why: a newer version (typing) is evaluated at once; killed by every burst row

name: S09 createCellContextScheduler: a version not below the evaluated one counts as evaluated
why: a document replaced by an older text is taken for evaluated; killed by the 'version lower than the one last evaluated' row

name: S10 createCellContextScheduler: an immediate evaluation leaves the pending run
why: the cancelled run still runs after an editor switch; killed by the editor-switch row (the count after the pause)

name: S11 createCellContextScheduler: evaluateNow works after dispose
why: an active-editor change after dispose evaluates; killed by the dispose row

name: S12 createCellContextScheduler: changed reads the editor after dispose
why: an event after dispose reads the active editor (the guard of evaluateNow and the disposed debouncer hide the rest); killed by the snapshot-reads counter

name: S13 createCellContextScheduler: dispose does not mark the scheduler disposed
why: an immediate event after dispose evaluates; killed by the dispose row

name: S14 createCellContextScheduler: dispose leaves the pending run
why: the pending evaluation runs after dispose; killed by the dispose-inside-the-window row

name: S15 createCellContextScheduler: the debounced run is the bare evaluator
why: the debounced evaluation records no version, so the next cursor move is debounced; killed by the 'cursor move after the burst's evaluation' row

name: S16 createCellContextScheduler: errors are not handed to onError
why: a debounced evaluation that throws goes to console.error; killed by the onError rows

name: S17 createCellContextScheduler: the debouncer runs on no delay
why: every pause row and the delay row

name: S18 createCellContextScheduler: the debouncer runs on the host's timers
why: the fake clock never sees a timer; killed by the sequence rows

name: S19 createCellContextScheduler: the choice is inverted
why: typing is evaluated at once and a cursor move is debounced

name: S20 createCellContextScheduler: an immediate event does not cancel the pending run
why: with no active editor an event evaluates but leaves the pending run; killed by the no-active-editor row

name: S21 createCellContextScheduler: evaluateNow is the bare evaluator
why: an active-editor change neither cancels the pending run nor honours dispose; killed by the editor-switch and dispose rows

name: T01 timeBurst: the burst is read as 0 ms

name: T05 the burst has no pause after the last keystroke

name: T06 the keystrokes are 1,000 ms apart

name: T07 the burst counts two events a keystroke
why: the events counts

name: T08 the burst forgets the tint's document event

name: F02 the fake clock breaks ties by the latest creation

name: F03 the fake clock does not move to the end of the window

why: the fake clock's stale-clear row
